Name: Adobe Acrobat Pro
Notes: Adobe ships a full native macOS build of Acrobat Pro - the exact equivalent. Preview (built into macOS) already merges, signs and annotates PDFs for free.

Name: Advanced IP Scanner
Notes: Scans IPs + ports with a GUI. Hardcoded in the manifest and installer.

Name: Advanced Port Scanner
Notes: Fast port scanning. nmap runs natively on macOS.

Name: Telegram
Notes: Official native macOS client (a separate Swift app - not an Electron wrapper).

Name: Terminator
Notes: iTerm2 is the macOS power-user terminal: split panes, profiles, search, tmux integration.

Name: WindTerm
Notes: Fast SSH/Telnet/Serial client with a file manager; official macOS build.

Name: WinDirStat
Notes: Disk-usage treemap - the macOS-native WinDirStat equivalent.

Name: PaperCut
macOS Package(s): PaperCut Print Deploy native macOS client
Notes: Hard-coded inclusion: install the NATIVE PaperCut macOS client, NEVER substitute plain CUPS. Download it from your own PaperCut server.

Name: Notepad++
macOS Package(s): bbedit (Cask) + sublime-text (Cask) + the real Notepad++ under Wine
Notes: Notepad++ is Windows-only. BBEdit is the classic macOS-native editor; the real Notepad++ can still run under Wine (64-bit installer only).

Name: PowerToys
macOS Package(s): rectangle (FancyZones) + raycast (PowerToys Run) + shottr (screen ruler/OCR) + hammerspoon (keyboard remap) + appcleaner
Source / URL: Homebrew Casks: rectangle, raycast, shottr, hammerspoon, appcleaner
Notes: Maps to several focused macOS tools, one per PowerToys feature; macOS itself already covers text extraction (Live Text), colour picking (Digital Colour Meter) and image resizing (Preview).

Name: WinRAR
Notes: WinRAR has no macOS GUI. Keka reads and writes RAR/7z/zip natively, and the official rar/unrar command line runs on macOS.

Name: Internet Download Manager (IDM)
Notes: IDM is Windows-only. Folx is the macOS-native download manager with browser integration; Free Download Manager is the free option.

Name: Microsoft 365 / Office
Notes: THE SAME Office you used on Windows: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and OneNote all have full native macOS builds. Sign in with the same account. LibreOffice remains the free fallback.

Name: Visual Studio Community 2026
Notes: Visual Studio for Mac was retired in 2024. VS Code with the C# Dev Kit, or JetBrains Rider, is the supported macOS path; the .NET SDK is fully native.

Name: Visual Studio Build Tools 2026
macOS Package(s): dotnet-sdk (Cask) + Xcode Command Line Tools + cmake/ninja (Homebrew)
Notes: The .NET SDK, clang/LLVM (via xcode-select --install) and CMake/Ninja give the same build toolchain natively on macOS.

Name: Adobe Digital Editions
Notes: Adobe Digital Editions has a native macOS build (Adobe DRM / ACSM support); Books is built into macOS and calibre manages the library.

Name: VMware Workstation
Notes: VMware Fusion is the macOS edition of Workstation and is free for personal use (a Broadcom account is needed for the download). Parallels Desktop and UTM are the alternatives.

Name: Gurobi
macOS Package(s): Gurobi macOS installer (commercial) + glpk / cbc (Homebrew formulae)
Notes: MANUAL section, commercial solver with a native macOS build. The free alternatives (glpk/cbc) install automatically first.

Name: SpotPlayer
Notes: MANUAL section with an explicit warning about the unverified source. Not auto-installed.

Name: RStudio
Notes: Posit ships a native macOS build (Apple Silicon supported); CRAN ships a native R.

Name: RealVNC Viewer
Notes: RealVNC Viewer has a native macOS build. macOS also has Screen Sharing built in (vnc:// URLs work out of the box).

Name: Pinta
Notes: Simple raster editor - the closest free macOS-native Paint.NET replacement (Acorn is the paid option).

Name: LanguageTool
Windows App?: No, best macOS alternative for Grammarly
In B_installed_windows_software.csv?: Yes (Grammarly CSV row present, LanguageTool listed as alternative)
Notes: Native macOS app plus Safari/Chrome extensions; the free, privacy-friendly Grammarly alternative.

Name: Proton VPN
Windows App?: No, best macOS alternative for Hotspot Shield / Psiphon
In B_installed_windows_software.csv?: Yes (Hotspot Shield / Psiphon CSV rows present, Proton VPN listed as alternative)
Notes: Official native macOS app. Replaces both Hotspot Shield and Psiphon.

Name: Wine
macOS Package(s): wine-stable (Homebrew Cask) + Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon
Notes: Windows compatibility layer, needed to run Windows-exclusive apps. It is an x86_64 build, so Apple Silicon needs Rosetta 2 (installed automatically). NOTE: macOS has had no 32-bit runtime since Catalina, so 32-bit Windows installers need CrossOver or a VM instead.

Name: CrossOver
Notes: Commercial, supported Wine with its own 32-bit layer and a Game Porting Toolkit backend - the route for Windows apps that plain Wine cannot run.

Name: Parallels Desktop
Notes: macOS-ONLY software. The smoothest way to keep running the handful of Windows apps that have no macOS build at all (Coherence mode puts them in the macOS Dock).

Name: UTM
Notes: Free QEMU/Apple-Virtualization front end - runs Linux and Windows-on-ARM VMs on Apple Silicon.

Name: VirtualBox
Notes: Oracle VirtualBox: full support on Intel Macs, developer preview on Apple Silicon.

Name: PostgreSQL
Windows App?: No, installed as a dependency for pgAdmin/pgNow workflows
In B_installed_windows_software.csv?: No (pgAdmin and pgNow ARE in CSV)
Notes: Postgres.app is the one-click macOS server; the Homebrew formula is the CLI/service route. Installed alongside pgAdmin for a full database environment.

Name: Docker Desktop
Windows App?: Yes, exists on Windows as Docker Desktop
macOS Package(s): docker-desktop (Homebrew Cask) or colima + docker (Homebrew formulae)
Notes: macOS runs containers inside a lightweight VM either way. Docker Desktop is the GUI option; colima is free, headless and works on both architectures.

Name: Homebrew
Notes: The package manager this whole toolkit installs applications with. execute_all.sh installs it (plus the Xcode Command Line Tools) on first run if it is missing.

Name: mas
Notes: Mac App Store command line, used for Store-only apps (Xcode, iMovie, Logic Pro, LINE, ...). You must be signed in to the App Store for it to work.

Name: Microsoft OneNote
In B_installed_windows_software.csv?: Yes (Microsoft To Do + Sticky Notes are in CSV)
Notes: OneNote has a free native macOS build and syncs the same notebooks. Apple Notes is built in, and Obsidian covers linked local-first notes.

Name: Sticky Notes
macOS Package(s): Stickies (built into macOS) + Notes (built into macOS)
Notes: Stickies is the macOS desktop sticky-note app; Notes syncs across your devices via iCloud. Nothing to install.

Name: CopyQ
Windows App?: No, best macOS alternative for Windows clipboard history
Notes: Clipboard manager with searchable history - the Win+V replacement. Set its hotkey in CopyQ > Preferences > Shortcuts (Command+Shift+V). Raycast and Alfred also keep clipboard history.

Name: Discord
Notes: Official native macOS client (voice/video/text chat).

Name: WhatsApp
Notes: WhatsApp ships an OFFICIAL native macOS app - unlike Linux, no unofficial wrapper is needed.

Name: Rectangle
Windows App?: No, best macOS alternative for Windows Snap / FancyZones
Notes: macOS had no Windows-style window snapping before Sequoia. Rectangle restores the keyboard-driven half/quarter tiling you are used to.

Name: Raycast
Windows App?: No, best macOS alternative for Windows Search / PowerToys Run
Notes: Spotlight replacement with clipboard history, window management, snippets and an extension store - the closest thing to PowerToys Run on macOS.
